name: Morning Glory Disc Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Morning Glory Disc Anomaly

criteria.description: Presence of an enlarged, funnel-shaped excavated optic disc
Peripapillary pigmentary changes or chorioretinal pigmentary disturbance
Central white glial tuft or membrane over the optic disc
Abnormal radial pattern of retinal vessels emerging from disc margin

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (enlarged excavated optic disc, surrounding pigmentary changes, and central glial tissue) must be present
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical based on fundoscopic examination; imaging may assist in confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Central white glial tuft on optic disc

rare.notes: Associated with midline craniofacial defects in some cases

imaging: Optical coherence tomography showing excavation of optic nerve head
Fundus photography demonstrating characteristic disc morphology
MRI brain to evaluate associated midline anomalies
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
other: Electroretinography may be normal or mildly affected

distinguishingFeatures: Coloboma typically has a notch or gap in the optic disc rather than a funnel-shaped excavation
Smaller, localized depressions near optic disc without central glial tuft
Usually no abnormal retinal vessel pattern
Small optic disc with reduced nerve fiber layer thickness

redFlags: Sudden vision loss or rapid deterioration
Neurological symptoms such as seizures or developmental delay
references: Hoyt CS, et al. Morning Glory Disc Anomaly. Surv Ophthalmol. 1977;22(4):271-283.
Mansour AM, et al. Clinical features and prognosis of morning glory syndrome. Ophthalmology. 1991;98(3): 345-350.
Orphanet: Morning Glory Disc Anomaly. Orphanet Report Series. 2020.
